question_text: An ideal air capacitor is charged to 10 V and isolated from all electrical connections. A dielectric with relative permittivity 4 is then inserted fully between its fixed plates. Ignore leakage and edge effects. What are the final voltage and the final stored electrical energy as a fraction of the initial energy?
explanation: Electrical isolation keeps charge fixed. A dielectric increases capacitance, so voltage and stored electrical energy fall at fixed charge. Vnew = Q/(4C) = 10/4 = 2.5 V. Unew/Uold = [Q²/(8C)]/[Q²/(2C)] = 1/4. The capacitance becomes four times larger while charge stays fixed, giving one quarter of the voltage and one quarter of the energy.

question_text: A node X is connected to +10 V through 1 kΩ and to ground through 1 kΩ. Diode D1 has its anode at X and cathode at an ideal +3 V reference. Diode D2 has its anode at an ideal +2 V reference and cathode at X. Both references can supply or absorb current. Use a 0.7 V forward drop and zero reverse current for each diode. What current flows through D1 in the steady state?
explanation: A diode-state assumption must agree with both its voltage polarity and the current balance at the node. With both diodes off, the divider gives VX = 5 V, which turns D1 on. Therefore VX = 3.7 V. D2 has anode-to-cathode voltage 2 - 3.7 = -1.7 V, so it is off. Upper current = 6.3 mA; lower current = 3.7 mA. ID1 = 6.3 - 3.7 = 2.6 mA, positive as required. D1 carries only the upper-resistor current left after supplying the lower resistor. The resulting positive current and reverse-biased D2 confirm the assumed states.
